claims.text: Astra is a conversational, reviewable BWB design loop from mission intent through geometry, aero, mesh, CFD and verdict.
Foam-Agent provides the inherited LangGraph CFD spine, RAG, case generation, execution, review and visualization workflow.
Astra adds the BWB domain pack, cockpit, design sessions, geometry, fast aero, deterministic meshing and result-quality gates.
The present project is aerodynamics-first conceptual design and excludes structural, propulsion, manufacturing and flight validation.
The design loop stages are mission, geometry, fast aero, mesh, CFD and evaluation.
Upstream revisions preserve version history and invalidate downstream results until rerun.
Evaluation combines convergence, plausibility, mission and visualization checks rather than trusting a clean solver exit.
Stage 1 distinguishes typed values, values in force and the bound that forced a change.
The golden verification brief records a 2 kg payload at 25 m/s cruise and 100 m altitude.
The recorded golden concept has 0.952 m2 reference area, 2.29 m span and aspect ratio 5.5.
The cockpit uses an instant browser preview while server-side validation and OpenVSP output remain authoritative.
The cockpit labels instant estimates separately from VSPAERO and CFD evidence.
Existing candidate designs can be browsed, screened and promoted through an explicit lifecycle.
The verified meshing path retains the watertight OpenVSP STL triangles as the aircraft boundary.
The farfield mesher uses deterministic Delaunay tetrahedralization and rejects zero-cell output.
Wall and symmetry patch types are fixed deterministically before case writing.
Netgen optimization reduced average non-orthogonality from 22.6 to 17.9 and maximum skewness from 2.6 to 1.5.
The verification report identifies the surface-pressure distribution and leading-edge suction region in the rendered case.
The verification report identifies stagnation, acceleration over the body and the wake in the symmetry-plane velocity slice.
The completed verification case reached residual levels in the 1e-5 to 1e-6 range.
The coarse CFD lift coefficient was 0.065 against a required 0.181.
The recorded coarse result had near-wall resolution of approximately y+ 900 and was treated as under-resolved.
The evaluator routed the completed case to revise-design rather than reporting a false pass.
Probabilistic routing and generated configuration are backed by deterministic validation, fallbacks and gates.
A controlled laminar comparison on the same geometry identified the mesh as the divergence source in the documented verification campaign.
A controlled coarse, medium and fine mesh study is the next experiment for reducing the largest aerodynamic uncertainty.
claims.sensitivity: Compare lift, force stability and near-wall resolution across mesh tiers.
claims.falsified_by: Refinement does not narrow the model disagreement or improve the near-wall evidence.
